papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and machine learning analyses to identify a prognostic signature based on tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), revealing potential therapeutic targets. The findings link TDT-related molecular features to patient outcomes, offering a new tool for risk stratification and treatment guidance in HNSCC.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This study benchmarks computational tools for analyzing nanopore long-read single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data, using matched short-read and long-read datasets. It provides a systematic comparison to guide tool selection for isoform detection in these emerging technologies.

papers.title: AI-driven discovery and validation of a GIPC1 PDZ domain inhibitor for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains highly aggressive, with a five-year survival rate under 13.3%, due to late diagnosis, rapid progression, and therapeutic resistance, highlighting the need for advanced treatments. GAIP-interacting protein C terminus 1 (GIPC1), a scaffolding protein overexpressed in PDAC, drives tumor growth and chemoresistance but has remained "undruggable" due to its PDZ domain. Using advanced computational modeling, machine learning, and predictive analytics, we identified a selective and specific small molecule inhibitor of GIPC1 (GIPCi) targeting its PDZ doma
papers.summary: This study uses AI-driven computational modeling and machine learning to identify a small molecule inhibitor (GIPCi) that targets the PDZ domain of GIPC1, a scaffolding protein overexpressed in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). The inhibitor shows selective binding and potential to block GIPC1's tumor-promoting and chemoresistance functions, offering a new therapeutic avenue for this aggressive cancer.

papers.title: Unraveling the roles of DKK1 and S100P in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: Insights from machine learning, single-cell/spatial transcriptomics, and functional validation.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with a 5-year survival rate of only 13%. Despite recent advances in diagnosis and treatment, the prognosis of PDAC remains poor, largely owing to its complex tumor microenvironment, epithelial heterogeneity, and therapeutic resistance. In this study, we integrated bulk transcriptomic datasets, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics (ST), machine learning analysis, and functional validation to investigate candidate biomarkers associated with PDAC progression. By intersecting genes selected using L
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify DKK1 and S100P as potential biomarkers associated with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma progression. The findings highlight their roles in the tumor microenvironment and suggest they may serve as therapeutic targets, with functional validation supporting their significance.

papers.title: Decoding Cardiac Development and Maturation at Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomic Resolution.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell transcriptomics have revolutionized our understanding of cardiac development and maturation by resolving cellular heterogeneity, delineating lineage trajectories, and uncovering gene regulatory networks and intercellular signaling at unprecedented resolution. The heart develops through a tightly coordinated spatiotemporal process that extends from early organogenesis through postnatal maturation. Despite major progress, key questions remain unresolved, including the localization and function of rare progenitor populations and the mechanisms that guide cardiomyocy
papers.summary: This review discusses how single-cell and spatial transcriptomics have advanced our understanding of cardiac development and maturation, highlighting the resolution of cellular heterogeneity, lineage trajectories, and gene regulatory networks. It also identifies unresolved questions, such as the roles of rare progenitor populations and mechanisms of cardiomyocyte maturation.

papers.title: MZB1 marks a B-cell-associated stromal-immune microenvironment in cervical squamous cell carcinoma: a multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) is a common gynecologic malignancy with a heterogeneous tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). The role of MZB1, a B-cell-specific molecular chaperone, in CSCC remains poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics analysis to characterize the role of MZB1 in cervical squamous cell carcinoma, finding that MZB1 marks a distinct B-cell-associated stromal-immune microenvironment. The results suggest MZB1 could serve as a biomarker for a specific tumor immune microenvironment subtype, potentially informing prognosis or immunotherapy response.

papers.title: A Multi-omics Regulated Cell Death Framework Defines Immune Phenotypes and Guides Precision Therapy in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is molecularly and immunologically heterogeneous, contributing to variable treatment response. Because regulated cell death (RCD) intersects with tumor metabolism, immune regulation, and therapeutic susceptibility, we built an RCD-centered framework for CRC stratification. Multi-cohort transcriptomic data were used to infer RCD subtypes with non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) and non-negative least squares (NNLS). Genomic, bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, and spatial transcriptomic datasets were integrated to characterize subtype-associated biology. Machine-learn
papers.summary: This study develops a multi-omics framework for colorectal cancer (CRC) that classifies tumors into regulated cell death (RCD) subtypes using transcriptomic data and machine learning. The subtypes are characterized by distinct immune phenotypes and genomic features, and the framework shows potential for guiding precision therapy decisions in CRC.

papers.title: NicheDeSig: Niche-aware Deconvolution and Adaptive Signature Analysis for Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: For spot-based spatial transcriptomics (ST), accurate cell-type deconvolution is essential for downstream analysis since each spot captures mixtures of multiple cell types. Meanwhile, spatial niches define distinct micro-environmental contexts, also salient for biological interpretation. However, existing deconvolution methods usually rely on fixed reference signatures or mapping single cells onto ST spots, without incorporating niche priors or modelling niche-dependent shifts. Consequently, existing methods remain focused on spot-level proportion estimation, with limited ability to support fu
papers.summary: NicheDeSig is a new computational method for spatial transcriptomics that performs cell-type deconvolution while incorporating spatial niche information, allowing it to model niche-dependent shifts in gene expression signatures. This approach improves accuracy of cell-type proportion estimates and enables adaptive signature analysis, addressing limitations of existing deconvolution tools that rely on fixed reference signatures.

papers.title: SPAE: Deciphering Cell Cycle Dynamics and Cell States in Single-cell RNA-seq Data.
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology have enabled the investigation of gene expression changes at the single-cell level, particularly for elucidating the heterogeneity among cells and complex biological processes. This technique reveals subtle molecular differences within individual cells, thereby offering a unique viewpoint for the investigation of cell cycle progression, cellular differentiation, and disease pathogenesis. However, accurately identifying and analyzing cell cycle dynamics in scRNA-seq data remains challenging due to the complexity of the data and
papers.summary: This paper introduces SPAE, a new computational method for deciphering cell cycle dynamics and cell states from single-cell RNA-seq data. It addresses the challenge of accurately identifying cell cycle phases in complex scRNA-seq datasets, offering a tool to better understand cellular heterogeneity and biological processes.

papers.title: CellCover defines marker gene panels capturing developmental progression in neocortical neural stem cell identity.
papers.abstract: Defining cell classes is central to the analysis of growing single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlases. Marker genes are most often identified by differential expression (DE) methods that assess genes one at a time, ignoring the redundancy and complementarity revealed when genes are considered jointly. Working with binarized expression data, we instead seek discriminating panels of genes that together are specific to a cell type, framing marker-panel selection as a variant of the minimal set-covering problem in combinatorial optimization. This formulation efficiently searches the vast spac
papers.summary: CellCover is a new computational method that selects panels of marker genes for cell types by treating the problem as a minimal set-cover, rather than relying on one-gene-at-a-time differential expression. Applied to neocortical neural stem cell data, it captures developmental progression more effectively than traditional marker gene approaches. This offers a more efficient and biologically informative way to define cell identities in single-cell atlases.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics uncover a THBS2⁺ CAF-KRT17⁺ malignant cell axis drives progression and immunotherapy resistance in pancreatic cancer.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) features a fibrotic stroma dominated by cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), yet the functional heterogeneity of CAFs and their crosstalk with malignant cells in metastasis and immune evasion remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize the tumor microenvironment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, identifying a specific interaction between THBS2-positive cancer-associated fibroblasts and KRT17-positive malignant cells that promotes tumor progression and resistance to immunotherapy. The findings reveal a novel cellular axis that could serve as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: An Integrated Transcriptional and Post-Transcriptional Regulatory Circuit Orchestrated by NUDT21 Maintains the Proliferation and Survival of Neuroblastoma.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor, associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study identifies NUDT21 as a key regulator of alternative polyadenylation in neuroblastoma, revealing an integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional circuit that maintains tumor cell proliferation and survival. The findings highlight APA as a critical mechanism in neuroblastoma pathogenesis and a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Pasta, a Versatile Transcriptomic Clock, Maps the Chemical and Genetic Determinants of Aging and Rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: With the growing burden of age-related diseases, understanding and modulating the aging process has become a priority. Transcriptomic aging clocks (TACs) can track biological age but remain limited by platform dependence, tissue specificity, or restricted accessibility. To address this, we developed Pasta, a robust and broadly applicable human TAC, built using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework. Pasta accurately predicted relative age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq as well as microarray data. Its predictions aligned with senescent and stem-lik
papers.summary: The authors developed Pasta, a versatile transcriptomic aging clock that accurately predicts biological age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-seq and microarray data. Using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework, Pasta maps chemical and genetic determinants of aging and rejuvenation, offering a broadly applicable tool for aging research.

papers.title: Loom: Multi-Region Analysis of Spatial Transcriptomics with Local Neighborhoods and Global Trajectories.
papers.abstract: We present Loom, a spatial transcriptomics (ST) visual computing system to support the analysis of pseudo-temporal trajectories, comparative investigation across samples and regions of interest, and the examination of spatially structured processes within local microenvironments. ST is a molecular profiling technology that measures gene expression directly within a thin tissue section while preserving its spatial organization. For practical application-driven analyses, the ST local microenvironment data needs to be integrated with cell reference datasets and temporal simulations of cell behavi
papers.summary: Loom is a new visual computing system for spatial transcriptomics that enables analysis of pseudo-temporal trajectories, cross-sample comparisons, and local microenvironment examination. It integrates spatial gene expression data with cell reference datasets and temporal simulations to support practical, application-driven analyses.

papers.title: An automated platform for spatial functional modeling and fingerprint analysis of tissue molecular landscapes.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables high-resolution molecular profiling while preserving tissue architecture, creating new opportunities to investigate how disease-associated pathways are organized within tissues. However, existing analytical approaches largely focus on individual pathways or cell types and do not provide a unified framework for modeling spatially varying pathway interactions across tissue sections and anatomical planes. We present an integrative framework, Spatial Fingerprints Analytics (SFinx), that introduces the concept of a spatial fingerprint for representing patterns o
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces SFinx, an automated platform that models spatial molecular landscapes in tissues by generating 'spatial fingerprints'—unified representations of pathway interactions across tissue sections. It provides a framework to analyze how disease-associated pathways are organized spatially, overcoming limitations of existing methods that focus on individual pathways or cell types.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses the emerging field of spatial biology in cancer epigenetics, highlighting how spatial transcriptomics and related technologies are being used to study epigenetic regulation within the tumor microenvironment. It emphasizes the importance of preserving tissue architecture to understand how spatially restricted regulatory programs influence cancer development and progression.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: This study presents a unified developmental timeline of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye by applying a gentle hydrogen peroxide-based bleaching method compatible with immunohistochemistry, enabling simultaneous analysis of melanin-containing structures. The authors generated a comprehensive atlas of pigmented ocular tissues and re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq data to provide a coordinated view of their development.

papers.title: A multimodal interrogation of Broca's area in the pediatric and adult human brain.
papers.abstract: Language is a defining trait of our species, and disruptions in language acquisition can have profound consequences to the individuals affected. Uncovering the neurodevelopmental basis of this complex trait requires detailed molecular and cellular insights into the neocortical areas that support linguistic abilities. Here we performed joint gene expression and chromatin accessibility profiling at single-nucleus resolution (10x Genomics Single cell Multiome) and spatial transcriptomic profiling (Xenium high-plex in situ spatial transcriptomics) of Broca's area alongside adjacent motor cortical
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint provides a multimodal single-cell and spatial atlas of Broca's area in pediatric and adult human brains, jointly profiling gene expression and chromatin accessibility alongside spatial transcriptomics. The study offers detailed molecular and cellular insights into the neocortical regions supporting language, potentially revealing developmental changes and cell-type-specific regulatory programs.

papers.title: A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, catalyzed by Adenosine Deaminases Acting on RNA (ADARs), is a widespread modification involved in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer. The Alu Editing Index (AEI) is the standard metric to estimate ADAR activity but requires raw sequencing reads and is poorly suited for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This study aimed to develop an alternative framework for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data across diverse transcriptomic technologies.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: This paper introduces a contextual activity score (CAS) to infer ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data, overcoming limitations of the standard Alu Editing Index (AEI) which requires raw reads and is unsuitable for single-cell or spatial data. The CAS enables ADAR activity estimation across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics, broadening applicability in studies of neural function, immunity, and cancer.

papers.title: Decoding neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts unveils a shared target reservoir for immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Primary liver cancer, predominantly hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), has limited therapeutic options. While mutation-derived neoantigen vaccine holds promise, its success is hindered by low antigen availability. This study explores transcriptome-derived neoantigens (neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts, neoTSTs) in HCC, characterizing their features, generation mechanisms, and therapeutic potential.
papers.summary: This study explores transcriptome-derived neoantigens (neoTSTs) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), identifying a shared reservoir of tumor-specific transcripts that could serve as targets for immunotherapy. The findings suggest that neoTSTs may overcome the limitation of low mutation-derived antigen availability, offering a promising avenue for vaccine development in HCC.

papers.title: Organism-scale annotation with Pan-human Azimuth.
papers.abstract: Single-cell atlases now span many human tissues, but inconsistent annotations across studies limit their utility as a unified reference. We introduce Pan-human Azimuth, a supervised neural network that maps human cells from diverse tissues and datasets onto a single hierarchical organism-scale typology. Developed through NIH HuBMAP, the model is trained on a uniquely curated corpus designed to maximize diversity across tissues and technologies while enforcing uniform, interpretable annotations and stringent quality control. The use of a single organism-wide reference enables us to map tens of
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Pan-human Azimuth is a supervised neural network that maps human cells from diverse tissues and datasets onto a single hierarchical organism-scale typology, addressing inconsistent annotations across single-cell atlases. Trained on a curated corpus from NIH HuBMAP, it provides uniform, interpretable annotations and stringent quality control, enabling organism-wide cell mapping.

papers.title: Human Myometrial Cell Fate under Chronic Oxidative Stress for Leiomyomagenesis.
papers.abstract: Uterine Leiomyoma are the most common benign tumors in women of reproductive age. Studies show that both leiomyoma and surrounding myometrium exist in a state of high oxidative stress, characterized by reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and impaired antioxidant defenses including defects of manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD). Oxidative stress has been proposed as a driver of leiomyoma initiation by promoting oxidative DNA damage leading to mutations in MED12 and leiomyoma growth. We hypothesize that chronic oxidative stress in human myometrial cells induces cellular remodeling and ge
papers.summary: This preprint investigates how chronic oxidative stress may drive the initiation of uterine leiomyomas by causing cellular remodeling in human myometrial cells. The authors hypothesize that oxidative stress promotes DNA damage and mutations, such as those in MED12, leading to tumor development. The study provides a potential mechanistic link between oxidative stress and leiomyoma pathogenesis.

papers.title: Autoreactive B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus: insights from integrative multi-omics analyses.
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by the emergence of autoantibodies and deposition of immune complexes. SLE presents with heterogeneous multi-organ involvement that varies among patients and its mechanisms have been investigated to facilitate appropriate stratification and treatment selection. Bulk RNA-seq and bulk ATAC-seq have provided important insights into the pathogenesis of SLE; however, these approaches are inherently limited by their reliance on predefined cell subsets and known markers, which can introduce bias and restrict their ability to fu
papers.summary: This review discusses how integrative multi-omics analyses, including bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq, have advanced understanding of autoreactive B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), while highlighting the limitations of these approaches due to reliance on predefined cell subsets. It emphasizes the need for unbiased, single-cell-level strategies to better capture disease heterogeneity and improve patient stratification and treatment selection.

papers.title: Robust and generalizable CNV detection for single-cell sequencing assays.
papers.abstract: Copy number variations (CNVs) are genomic structural variants that are strongly linked to cancer progression and genetic disorders. CNVs can be highly heterogeneous at population and tissue scale; thus, single-cell resolution detection holds great promise for studying clonal evolution and CNV-driven changes. Despite advanced sc-RNA-seq CNV detection methods, accurate methods for epigenomic single-cell modalities lag behind. We developed RIDDLER; a robust, unsupervised method that uses outlier-aware statistical modeling to detect CNVs across multiple single-cell modalities and assays. RIDDLER u
papers.summary: This paper presents RIDDLER, a new computational method for detecting copy number variations (CNVs) in single-cell sequencing data. Unlike existing tools, RIDDLER is robust and generalizable across multiple single-cell modalities, including epigenomic assays, using an unsupervised, outlier-aware statistical approach. This addresses a critical gap in single-cell CNV detection, particularly for epigenomic data.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses a single-cell CRISPR screen (CROP-seq) to identify epigenetic regulators essential for pluripotency in mouse embryonic stem cells. The authors uncover an antagonistic relationship between Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3 that orchestrates the transition between naive and primed pluripotency states.

papers.title: Reference Regulatory Element-Guided Gene Expression Analysis for Mechanistic Inference of Gene Regulatory Networks.
papers.abstract: Regulatory genomics faces a depth-breadth gap: deep multi-omics provides regulatory detail but is difficult to scale, whereas broad expression datasets often lack the regulatory structure needed for mechanistic Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) analysis. We developed Regulatory Elements Guided Analysis (REGA), an interpretable framework that uses reference Regulatory Element (RE) catalogs to infer transcription factor (TF)-RE-gene programs from gene expression data. Across ChIP-seq, knockdown, Hi-C, cis- and trans-eQTL benchmarks, REGA prioritized functional REs, improved RE-gene and TF-gene infer
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: REGA is a new computational framework that uses reference regulatory element catalogs to infer transcription factor-regulatory element-gene programs from gene expression data, bridging the gap between deep multi-omics and broad expression datasets. It improves the prioritization of functional regulatory elements and enhances gene regulatory network inference, as validated across multiple benchmarks including ChIP-seq, knockdown, Hi-C, and eQTL data.

papers.title: Spatial Topology Reveals Biologically Distinct Recurrent Motifs in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Most spatial transcriptomic analyses of solid tumors focus on individual cell states or single-sample spatial domains rather than on recurrent multicellular tissue architectures shared across patients, and typically depend on predefined cell-type annotations or compartment definitions. We developed STORM (Spatial Topology analysis of Recurrent Motifs), an unsupervised graph-attention variational autoencoder that learns recurrent spatial motifs directly from cell-level graph structure and molecular profiles without cell-type labels, manual annotation, or predefined compartments. We applied to 3
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces STORM, an unsupervised graph-attention variational autoencoder that identifies recurrent multicellular spatial motifs directly from spatial transcriptomics data without requiring cell-type labels or predefined compartments. Applied to colorectal cancer samples, STORM reveals biologically distinct recurrent motifs that may represent shared tumor architectures across patients, offering a new approach to analyzing spatial organization in solid tumors.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics reveal mechanistic insights of FOLH1+ endothelial cells in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most prevalent and aggressive subtype of renal malignancy, characterized by extensive vascularization and poor prognosis. Early detection markedly improves patient outcomes, and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA, encoded by FOLH1) imaging has recently emerged as a valuable diagnostic tool for ccRCC. However, the cellular source, spatial distribution, and mechanistic contribution of FOLH1 expression within the tumor microenvironment remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial multi-omics to characterize FOLH1+ endothelial cells in clear cell renal cell carcinoma, revealing their cellular source, spatial distribution, and potential mechanistic roles in the tumor microenvironment. The findings provide new insights into how FOLH1 expression in endothelial cells may contribute to tumor vascularization and could inform PSMA-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Scalable hypothalamic neuron differentiation from human pluripotent stem cells suitable for modeling metabolic disorders.
papers.abstract: The hypothalamus, composed of multiple nuclei, is essential for maintaining the body's homeostasis. Within the mediobasal hypothalamus, the arcuate nucleus (ARC) contains key neuronal populations, including appetite-suppressing pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons that regulate energy and glucose balance. Here, we present a chemically defined, scalable method for differentiating human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) into hypothalamic neurons enriched for POMC cells, compatible with robotic cell culture platforms for high-throughput use. Neuronal identity was validated by MERFISH single-cell tran
papers.summary: This paper presents a scalable, chemically defined method for differentiating human pluripotent stem cells into hypothalamic neurons enriched for appetite-regulating POMC neurons, compatible with robotic platforms for high-throughput screening. The approach enables modeling of metabolic disorders and was validated using MERFISH single-cell transcriptomics.

papers.title: Functional Depth Biomarkers Distinguish Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma from Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) exhibit fundamentally distinct pathway coordination architectures. We developed a framework integrating pathway activity inference from spatial transcriptomics data, spatial proximity based network construction, and functional depth analysis across 996 TCGA patients. Applying Fraiman-Muniz depth statistics, we generated two representations: Population Referenced Depth quantifies typicality relative to population distributions, while Patient Referenced Depth assesses within-patient network organization. Random forest classificat
papers.summary: This study introduces a framework that integrates spatial transcriptomics-derived pathway activity with functional depth analysis to distinguish lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) from lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Using Fraiman-Muniz depth statistics on TCGA data, the authors generate two depth representations and apply random forest classification, achieving accurate discrimination based on pathway coordination architecture.

papers.title: Identification of potential diagnostic biomarkers for myocardial infarction using bioinformatics and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction(AMI)is an important type of cardiovascular disease, which seriously threatens the lives of humans. In order to help patients receive timely clinical treatment and improve their survival rates, it is necessary to screen out related molecules in advance. To this end, we applied bioinformatics methods and machine learning algorithms to find possible biomarkers associated with AMI. When considering possible connections with dynamics of immune cells activation. Based on the RNA-seq results, differential expression analysis was performed followed by WGCNA to identify stab
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatics and machine learning to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers for acute myocardial infarction (AMI), with a focus on immune cell dynamics. The authors performed differential expression analysis and WGCNA on RNA-seq data to screen for candidate molecules, which could aid in earlier diagnosis and treatment.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics identifies CYP1B1 as a candidate molecular link between toxicant exposure and ferroptosis-related epithelial stress in COPD.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by progressive airflow limitation, chronic airway inflammation, and epithelial remodeling. Although oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation are increasingly recognized as important contributors to COPD pathobiology, the epithelial biomarkers and regulatory pathways linking cigarette-smoke exposure to ferroptosis-related injury remain incompletely defined.
papers.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
papers.summary: This study uses an integrative multi-omics approach to identify CYP1B1 as a potential molecular link between toxicant exposure and ferroptosis-related epithelial stress in COPD. The findings suggest that CYP1B1 may serve as a biomarker and therapeutic target in COPD pathogenesis.

papers.title: PathwayBench: a multi-criterion benchmark of pseudobulk pathway activity scoring methods reveals rank-window competition as a mechanism of biological signal loss in single-cell RNA-seq.
papers.abstract: Pathway activity scoring is a foundational step in single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) analysis, yet method choice is rarely guided by systematic, multi-criterion evidence in the pseudobulk case-control regime that now dominates applied single-cell disease studies. Prior single-cell pathway-scoring benchmarks have focused on perturbation ground truth at cell-level resolution, leaving the donor-level pseudobulk setting - and the question of why methods disagree - largely unaddressed.
papers.summary: This paper introduces PathwayBench, a multi-criterion benchmark for evaluating pseudobulk pathway activity scoring methods in single-cell RNA-seq case-control studies. The authors identify 'rank-window competition' as a mechanism causing biological signal loss, providing systematic evidence to guide method selection in this common analysis regime.

papers.title: KNOX1 Transcription Factors in Plants with a Special Focus on Horticultural Crops: A Review.
papers.abstract: Class I KNOX1 (KNOTTED1-like homeobox 1) transcription factors integrate gibberellin (GA), cytokinin (CK), and auxin (IAA) signaling to maintain shoot apical meristem identity and coordinate plant organogenesis. This review examines the structural conservation, evolutionary dynamics, and regulatory architecture of KNOX1 genes across horticultural crops, drawing essential mechanistic context from model species. We synthesize KNOX1 functions in six agronomic domains, including plant architecture and branching, leaf morphogenesis and ornamental traits, floral development and sex determination, fr
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on Class I KNOX1 transcription factors in plants, focusing on their roles in hormone signaling integration and organ development, with particular emphasis on horticultural crops. It covers structural conservation, evolutionary dynamics, and regulatory functions across six agronomic domains, providing a comprehensive resource for understanding KNOX1-mediated control of plant architecture and development.

papers.title: Circadian Gene Networks and Transcriptome Oscillations in Prostate Cancer: Insights From RNA Sequencing and Implications for Chronotherapy.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer is increasingly recognized as a disease influenced not only by genetic and molecular alterations but also by disruption of circadian regulatory networks. Advances in RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) have enabled transcriptome-wide investigation of temporal gene expression patterns, revealing complex interactions between core clock genes, androgen receptor signaling, alternative splicing, and metabolic pathways. Emerging evidence suggests that circadian dysregulation contributes to prostate cancer progression through alterations in gene expression, transcript isoform remodeling, and tre
papers.summary: This review discusses how circadian gene networks and transcriptome oscillations contribute to prostate cancer progression, highlighting RNA sequencing studies that reveal interactions between core clock genes, androgen receptor signaling, and metabolic pathways. It also explores the potential of chronotherapy—timing treatment to the body's circadian rhythms—as a strategy to improve therapeutic outcomes.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomic analysis reveals spatial features in human Stanford type A aortic dissection.
papers.abstract: Stanford type A aortic dissection (AAD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular disease characterized by tearing in the aortic wall. Using spatial transcriptomics and multiplex immunofluorescence, we comprehensively analyzed ascending aortas from eight AAD patients across different severities and segments. We demonstrate that SPP1-driven inflammatory signaling intensifies with AAD severity, identifying a nine-gene, layer-anchored severity scale: MYL6/CALD1/MYH9 (mild); CCL2/CP/COL4A1 (moderate); and TMSB4X/ATP5F1E/PKM (severe). Importantly, the collagen-remodeling triad COL1A1/COL3A1/MMP2 is conc
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics and multiplex immunofluorescence to map gene expression across ascending aortas from eight patients with Stanford type A aortic dissection (AAD), revealing that SPP1-driven inflammatory signaling increases with disease severity. The authors identify a nine-gene, layer-anchored severity scale and a collagen-remodeling triad (COL1A1/COL3A1/MMP2) that may serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Multiomics identifies a prognostic signature and SPIB as a potential regulator of gastric cancer lymph node metastasis.
papers.abstract: The heterogeneity within the same AJCC TNM stage of gastric cancer necessitates robust prognostic biomarkers beyond conventional staging. By integrating transcriptomic data from 1,613 patients across eight cohorts, we developed an 11-gene lymph node metastasis gene signature (LMGS) using an ensemble learning strategy to overcome the instability of traditional models. LMGS robustly predicted survival (mean C-index = 0.619), providing incremental prognostic value beyond conventional AJCC staging. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses revealed LMGS enrichment in epithelial/immune cells
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data from 1,613 gastric cancer patients to develop an 11-gene lymph node metastasis signature (LMGS) that improves survival prediction beyond conventional staging. Single-cell and spatial analyses implicate SPIB as a potential regulator of lymph node metastasis, offering new insights into gastric cancer biology and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Lineage-calibrated peripheral monocyte-derived myeloid states in neurodegenerative disease: Recruitment, lesion decoding, and state persistence.
papers.abstract: Peripheral monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages are increasingly implicated in neurodegenerative disease, yet interpretation remains limited by phenotypic convergence with resident microglia, inconsistent lineage attribution, and strong dependence on experimental model and disease stage. We present a structured, lineage-calibrated framework that separates three linked processes: a recruitment gate controlling access to CNS borders and lesions; a lesion-decoding hub through which aggregate, lipid, cytokine, complement, antigenic, hypoxic, and danger-associated inputs are interpreted; and
papers.summary: This paper presents a structured framework for understanding how peripheral monocytes contribute to neurodegenerative disease, distinguishing them from resident microglia and clarifying their roles in recruitment, lesion response, and persistence. It provides a lineage-calibrated approach that could improve interpretation of myeloid cell states across disease stages and models.

papers.title: Ligand-based directed differentiation to produce granulosa-like cells expressing steroidogenic enzyme genes.
papers.abstract: The ovarian granulosa cells are responsible for producing hormones and supporting oocytes through maturation and meiotic resumption. There is a need to generate granulosa-like cells (GLCs) from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) to better model human gonadal development and to test the effects of exogenous or pharmaceutical compounds on the ovary. Here we report a rapid ligand-based protocol for differentiating hiPSCs into cells that express markers of the transient developmental lineages and steroidogenic pathway genes. Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified can
papers.summary: This paper describes a rapid, ligand-based protocol for differentiating human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) into granulosa-like cells (GLCs) that express steroidogenic enzyme genes, providing a new in vitro model for studying ovarian development and testing pharmaceutical effects. The authors used single-cell RNA-sequencing to characterize the differentiated cells and confirm their identity.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics supports a role for SOX4-driven signaling throughout the disease course of biliary atresia.
papers.abstract: Biliary atresia (BA) is a neonatal fibroinflammatory cholangiopathy of infancy and the most common indication for pediatric liver transplantation. We aimed to define the molecular mechanisms responsible for differences in the rate of disease progression among children with BA.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to investigate biliary atresia (BA), a neonatal liver disease, and identifies SOX4-driven signaling as a key pathway active throughout the disease course. The findings suggest that SOX4 may contribute to the variable progression rates seen in BA patients, offering a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Discovery of hub genes linking oxidative stress to type 2 diabetic sarcopenia using single-cell sequencing and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and sarcopenia demonstrate a significant comorbidity, particularly in the elderly, yet the molecular mechanisms linking them, especially through oxidative stress, remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify oxidative stress-related hub genes involved in T2DM-associated sarcopenia (T2DS) by integrating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and bulk RNA-seq data with machine learning. We analyzed scRNA-seq datasets (GSE244515, GSE268953) to characterize cellular heterogeneity and bulk RNA-seq datasets (GSE202295, GSE226151) for differential expre
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data with machine learning to identify oxidative stress-related hub genes that may link type 2 diabetes mellitus and sarcopenia. The findings provide candidate molecular targets and insights into the shared pathophysiology of these comorbid conditions, particularly in the elderly.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals an SPP1-centered immune-fibrotic axis associated with fibrosis-related tissue remodeling in IgG4-related disease.
papers.abstract: IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a fibroinflammatory condition characterized by progressive organ damage; however, the spatial organization linking immune dysregulation to fibrotic remodeling remains incompletely understood. In this study, we performed spatial transcriptomic analysis of submandibular gland tissues from patients with IgG4-RD representing two distinct fibrosis-associated tissue states. Gene expression data were normalized and z-scored, and immune- and fibrosis-related module scores were calculated. Fibrotic niches were defined based on COL1A1 expression and fibroblast signature
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to map the cellular organization of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) in submandibular gland tissues, revealing an SPP1-centered immune-fibrotic axis that links immune dysregulation with fibrotic tissue remodeling. The findings identify distinct fibrosis-associated tissue states and define fibrotic niches, providing new insights into the spatial interplay between immune and fibrotic processes in IgG4-RD.

papers.title: Divergent cytotoxic and inflammatory functions of intratumoral Vδ2+ γδ T cells in renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Vγ9Vδ2 T cells are blood-circulating, innate-like lymphocytes that contribute to tumor immunosurveillance and constitute over 95% of Vδ2+ γδ T cells, but how they perform antitumor or protumor functions remains unclear. Here, we comprehensively characterized Vδ2+ γδ T cells in paired peripheral blood and tumor samples from patients with renal cell carcinoma using flow cytometry and single-cell transcriptomic analysis. We identified two major Vδ2+ γδ T cell subsets distinguished by expression of CD16, which were present at variable proportions in both circulation and tumors. Notably, the propor
papers.summary: This study characterizes Vδ2+ γδ T cells in renal cell carcinoma patients using flow cytometry and single-cell transcriptomics, identifying two major subsets defined by CD16 expression with divergent cytotoxic and inflammatory functions in tumors. The findings reveal how these innate-like lymphocytes may contribute to either antitumor or protumor responses depending on their subset composition.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomic analysis of kidney biopsies identifies activation of complement and SPP1 networks in Staphylococcus infection-associated glomerulonephritis.
papers.abstract: Staphylococcus infection-associated glomerulonephritis (SAGN) has emerged as the leading cause of infection-related glomerulonephritis (IRGN) in the Western subcontinents, but pathogenesis remains poorly understood in the absence of animal models and detailed molecular mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics on kidney biopsies from patients with Staphylococcus infection-associated glomerulonephritis (SAGN) to identify disease-specific molecular networks. The authors found activation of complement pathways and SPP1-related signaling, providing new insights into the pathogenesis of this condition.

papers.title: Gut microbiota induces immune-related alterations in gene expression, RNA methylation, and metabolism in glioblastoma revealed by single-cell and spatial multi-omics.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly malignant tumor with poor prognosis and limited effective treatment options. Emerging studies have suggested that gut microbiota may influence glioma progression through the gut-brain axis, though the precise mechanisms remain largely unclear. In this study, we employed a comprehensive multi-omics approach-encompassing single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, metagenomics, metabolomics, and m6A-seq-to investigate how antibiotic-induced gut microbiota disruption impacts glioma progression in a mouse model. Gene expression analysis revealed significant
papers.summary: This study uses a multi-omics approach (single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, metagenomics, metabolomics, and m6A-seq) to show that antibiotic-induced gut microbiota disruption alters gene expression, RNA methylation, and metabolism in a mouse glioblastoma model, providing evidence for gut-brain axis involvement in glioma progression. The findings suggest that the gut microbiome may influence tumor biology through immune-related and epigenetic mechanisms, offering potential new avenues for GBM therapy.

papers.title: Analysis of senescence in pituitary tumors from different lineages and the potential role of senolytic drugs as targeted therapies.
papers.abstract: Pituitary tumors (PT) constitute the second most frequent intracranial tumor. A subset of PT can behave aggressively despite multimodal treatment. Hallmarks such as cellular senescence, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and stemness have been implicated in tumor progression, but their role in PT pathogenesis remains is unclear.
papers.summary: This study analyzes markers of cellular senescence, EMT, and stemness in pituitary tumors across different lineages, finding that senescence is present but varies by tumor type. The authors suggest that senolytic drugs, which selectively eliminate senescent cells, could be a potential targeted therapy for aggressive pituitary tumors.

papers.title: A multi-omics framework integrating gut microbiota, blood metabolites, and immune cells to elucidate the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) develops through complex interactions between the central nervous system and peripheral systems. The microbiota-metabolite-immune axis has emerged as an important focus of AD research. However, the coordinated mechanisms that regulate this axis remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study presents a multi-omics framework that integrates gut microbiota, blood metabolites, and immune cells to investigate the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). By analyzing these interconnected layers, the authors identify coordinated mechanisms along the microbiota-metabolite-immune axis that may contribute to AD development, offering a more systems-level understanding of the disease.

papers.title: From proteome-wide Mendelian randomization and multi-omics integration to functional validation: TGFB3 as a prioritized candidate in gastric adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Gastric adenocarcinoma lacks robust circulating biomarkers and tractable targets. We assessed whether genetically predicted plasma protein levels influence disease risk and sought druggable candidates using a proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) framework.
papers.summary: This study uses proteome-wide Mendelian randomization to identify plasma proteins that may influence gastric adenocarcinoma risk, followed by multi-omics integration and functional validation. The authors prioritize TGFB3 as a candidate biomarker and potential therapeutic target, suggesting a novel avenue for early detection and treatment.

papers.title: Global research landscape and trends of single-cell sequencing in sexually transmitted infections: a comprehensive bibliometric analysis from 2015 to 2025.
papers.abstract: Single-cell sequencing offers new insights into sexually transmitted infections (STIs) research, but there remains a lack of systematic bibliometric overview. Here, we summarize and quantify the developmental dynamics, research hotspots, and future directions of single-cell sequencing in STIs through bibliometric analysis.
papers.summary: This paper provides a bibliometric analysis of single-cell sequencing research applied to sexually transmitted infections (STIs) from 2015 to 2025, mapping the field's growth, key contributors, and emerging topics. It identifies current research hotspots and future directions, offering a structured overview for researchers in this niche area.
